hyperedges.description: Together these nodes describe how the Bliss-style wallpaper anchors GooseOS's visual identity as a Win95/XP-era nostalgic desktop environment.

hyperedges.label: GooseOS Voting Carousel Scene (no-gods state)
hyperedges.description: All elements visible in the no-gods.png screenshot together form the GooseOS voting carousel scene: the Win95 desktop environment, the belle-lettres window, the carousel navigation, and the 'He attacc' goose meme submission with its caption.

hyperedges.label: GooseOS Voting UI Cluster
hyperedges.description: The ballot-lottery.exe window, voting carousel component, goose photo, and humorous caption together form the complete goose art voting interface in GooseOS.

hyperedges.label: Goose Art Upload UX Flow
hyperedges.description: The complete UX flow: user selects/drops an image via dropzone or browse button, adds a description in the text field, then clicks upload to submit the goose art.

hyperedges.label: Skeuomorphic CRT TV Design System
hyperedges.description: All visible UI elements within the CRT TV widget share a unified skeuomorphic retro-CRT design language: physical knob controls, analog static noise, green terminal text overlays, and a boxy vintage television form factor. Together these elements create a coherent lo-fi ambient TV viewing experience.

hyperedges.label: Win95 Desktop Shell Context
hyperedges.description: The window title bar, taskbar with './start' button, and desktop background collectively constitute the Win95-style desktop environment shell that wraps all GooseOS features including the Vibes CRT TV viewer.

nodes.label: VGOD Glitch Art Desktop Background
nodes.description: A wide-format background image featuring heavy glitch art aesthetics: dominant cyan/turquoise hues overlaid with purple and magenta chromatic aberration, vertical CRT scan-line distortion pattern, and a corrupted/distorted silhouette figure (animal or abstract form) rendered in the glitch style. Dark vignette border frames the composition.

nodes.label: Glitch Art Visual Aesthetic
nodes.description: The image employs deliberate digital corruption aesthetics: chromatic aberration splitting color channels, vertical scan-line interference reminiscent of CRT monitor artifacts, and pixelated color bleed. These are hallmarks of glitch art as a visual style.

nodes.label: CRT Scan-Line Distortion Pattern
nodes.description: Dark vertical lines overlay the entire image at regular intervals, simulating the scan-line pattern of a CRT display or analog video signal interference. This is a prominent and intentional retro-tech visual element.

nodes.label: Cyan-Dominant Vaporwave Color Palette
nodes.description: The image uses a vivid cyan/turquoise base with purple, magenta, and dark teal accents. This high-saturation, cool-warm contrast palette is characteristic of vaporwave and retro-futurist digital art movements.

nodes.label: Distorted Abstract Silhouette Figure
nodes.description: A dark, corrupted silhouette form occupies the center-left of the image. The glitch distortion makes its exact subject ambiguous — it could be an animal (goose-related given project context), a human figure, or a purely abstract shape. The distortion intentionally obscures the original subject.

nodes.label: Retro-Chaos Desktop Atmosphere Intent
nodes.description: The aggressive glitch aesthetic of this background image is likely chosen to complement the Win95-style desktop environment of GooseOS, amplifying its retro-chaos personality. The corruption and scan-line effects create a sense of digital irreverence that matches the project's playful, lo-fi brand.

nodes.label: Background Named After Visual/Cultural Reference (vgod)
nodes.description: The filename 'vgod' may reference 'vape god' (internet/meme culture), a gaming handle, or a creative alias, suggesting the background images in GooseOS are named after cultural references or creator identities rather than descriptive content — an informal, community-driven asset naming convention.

nodes.label: Dark Vignette Border Framing
nodes.description: A dark border or vignette frames the edges of the image, drawing focus to the glitched center and giving the background a contained, monitor-screen-within-a-monitor feeling — reinforcing the retro CRT display metaphor.

nodes.label: Windows XP Bliss Desktop Wallpaper
nodes.description: Photographic desktop wallpaper depicting a vivid green rolling grass hill under a bright blue sky with scattered white cumulus clouds. Closely matches the iconic Windows XP 'Bliss' default wallpaper.

nodes.label: Green Rolling Hill Foreground Element
nodes.description: Lush, saturated green grass hill occupying the lower half of the image, curving gently from lower-left to upper-center. Small yellow wildflowers are faintly visible near the bottom edge.

nodes.label: Blue Sky with White Cumulus Clouds
nodes.description: Vivid cerulean blue sky filling the upper portion of the image, populated with multiple white and light-grey cumulus and cirrus clouds of varying sizes.
nodes.norm_label: blue sky with white cumulus clouds

nodes.label: Distant Hills on Horizon
nodes.description: Low-lying hills and possibly tree-line visible in the far background on the right side of the horizon, providing depth and landscape context.

nodes.label: Windows XP Bliss Nostalgia Reference
nodes.description: The deliberate use of the Windows XP Bliss wallpaper (or a very close replica) reinforces the Win95/WinXP-era nostalgic aesthetic of the GooseOS desktop environment, signaling retro computing theming to users familiar with early-2000s personal computing.

nodes.label: Retro Desktop OS Aesthetic Design Decision
nodes.description: Choosing a wallpaper nearly identical to Windows XP Bliss is an intentional UI/UX pattern establishing GooseOS as a nostalgic parody or homage to classic Windows desktop environments, expected to evoke immediate recognition in users who grew up with Windows XP.
nodes.norm_label: retro desktop os aesthetic design decision

nodes.label: High Saturation Color Palette
nodes.description: The image uses highly saturated greens and blues, giving it an almost hyper-real photographic quality. Dominant colors: vivid green (#4caf50 range), bright sky blue (#2196f3 range), and pure white clouds.

nodes.label: Photographic Background Texture
nodes.description: The background is a photographic image (not illustrated or generated), providing a realistic textured backdrop contrasting with the flat/pixelated Win95-style UI chrome elements layered on top.

nodes.label: Background Layer for Desktop UI Composition
nodes.description: As a named 'backgrounds' asset, this image is intended to sit behind all other UI elements (windows, taskbar, icons), providing the full-screen desktop canvas typical of a windowed OS environment.
nodes.norm_label: background layer for desktop ui composition

nodes.label: GooseOS Favicon 16x16
nodes.description: A 16x16 pixel favicon depicting a small pixelated cartoon goose. The figure has a tan/brown body, a small beak, and simple limbs, rendered in the low-resolution style typical of browser favicons. Serves as the browser tab icon for the GooseOS Win95-style desktop environment.
nodes.visual_content: pixelated cartoon goose, brown/tan body, small beak, simple limbs

nodes.label: GooseOS Favicon 32x32
nodes.description: A 32x32 pixel favicon depicting a pixel-art style goose icon. The goose is rendered as a simple forward-facing figure with a white and grey body, an orange beak, and dark eye detail. The design is minimal and iconic, suitable for browser tab display, representing the GooseOS Win95-style desktop environment project.

nodes.label: Carousel Icon
nodes.description: A Win95-style desktop icon for the goose art voting carousel feature. The SVG depicts a slideshow/photo gallery interface: a large rounded-rectangle frame (light blue fill) containing a landscape image area with a sky-blue background, a circular sun/orb element (top-left), and two layered mountain or hill silhouettes in green tones. Behind and to the right is a second overlapping panel with a dashed border, suggesting a stack of slides. The composition visually communicates an image carousel or slideshow viewer, consistent with its use as the toolbar/taskbar icon for the GooseOS voting carousel window.
nodes.origin: SVG Repo (svgrepo.com), generated via SVG Repo Mixer Tools

nodes.label: Fairy Goose Icon
nodes.description: Black and white pen-and-ink style illustration depicting a small witch or gnome figure riding on the back of a large goose in flight. The rider wears a pointed pilgrim/witch hat and glasses, holds a broomstick aloft, and is dressed in old-fashioned buckled clothing. The goose has wide outstretched wings and faces left. The style is reminiscent of vintage storybook or woodcut engravings. Used as an icon in the GooseOS Win95-style desktop environment.
nodes.style: black and white pen-and-ink / woodcut engraving

nodes.label: Floppy Disk Icon
nodes.description: A Win95-style floppy disk SVG icon (800x800px, 1024 viewBox) sourced from SVG Repo. The icon features a yellow-green (#B8CA43) floppy disk body with a dark outline, a cream/off-white (#F8F4BC) label area on the upper portion, a darker olive-green (#7E8D69) lower storage section, and a yellow-green write-protect notch cutout (#B8CA43). Horizontal lines in the lower section represent data lines. Used as a UI icon in GooseOS, a Win95-style desktop environment.

nodes.label: Goose Game Icon
nodes.description: 800x800px SVG icon depicting a stylized cartoon goose with a rounded gray body, amber/brown beak and feet, elliptical dark eyes, and decorative chest/belly coloring. Used as the desktop icon for the Goose Game feature in the GooseOS Win95-style environment. Sourced from SVG Repo via the SVG Repo Mixer Tools generator.

nodes.label: Photos Icon
nodes.description: Win95-style photos/gallery icon depicting a landscape scene: a light-blue sky rectangle with a white sun and cloud shape in the upper-right, a white circle (sun or moon) in the upper-left, and two overlapping terrain/hill silhouettes in dark blue-grey at the bottom — representing a photo gallery or image viewer application icon.

nodes.label: Themes Icon
nodes.description: A color palette and paintbrush SVG icon used for the Themes/Customize entry in the GooseOS Win95-style desktop. The palette body is a large teardrop shape in golden yellow (#FEC656) with five multicolored paint swirls arranged around its surface in red (#F16D6E), green (#80C350), slate-blue (#637888), brown (#B06D48), and teal (#60C3AB). A paintbrush handle is rendered on the left side with a grey gradient barrel and a red bristle tip, consistent with classic Win95-era 'Display Properties / Themes' iconography. Sourced from SVG Repo (SVG Repo Mixer Tools). 800x800 viewBox scaled to 502.441x502.441 internal units.

nodes.label: TV Icon
nodes.description: A retro-style television set icon sourced from SVG Repo. The SVG depicts a gold/yellow TV cabinet body with a large cream/off-white screen on the left side showing a line graph or waveform (vibes/signal visualization), circular control knobs on the right side (a green channel/power knob with a cross indicator and three horizontal slider bars), and two diagonal antenna lines extending from the top. Used as the 'TV/vibes' desktop icon in the GooseOS Win95-style desktop environment.

nodes.label: GooseOS Main Desktop
nodes.description: Win95-style desktop environment showing the full GooseOS desktop with wallpaper, icons, and taskbar. Overall composition mimics classic Windows XP Bliss wallpaper aesthetic with rolling green hills and blue sky.

nodes.label: Windows XP Bliss-Style Wallpaper
nodes.description: Background wallpaper is a direct homage to the iconic Windows XP 'Bliss' wallpaper: rolling green grassy hill under a vivid blue sky with scattered white cumulus clouds. Occupies nearly the entire screen real estate behind the icons and taskbar.

nodes.label: Win95-Style Taskbar
nodes.description: Thin horizontal taskbar anchored to the bottom of the screen. Dark/charcoal background color. Contains a Start button labeled './start' on the far left, styled with retro terminal-script syntax ('./start') instead of a traditional 'Start' label, evoking a Unix shell command aesthetic fused with Win95 UI.

nodes.label: Start Button (./start)
nodes.description: The Start button in the bottom-left corner of the taskbar is labeled './start' — a Unix shell script invocation syntax replacing the classic 'Start' label. Small rectangular button with dark background and light text. This is a deliberate design choice merging terminal culture with Win95 UI metaphor.

nodes.label: Desktop Icon: //game.sh
nodes.description: Desktop icon in the upper-left area of the desktop. Icon image appears to be a small humanoid/robot figure (possibly a goose character). Label reads '//game.sh' — using double-slash prefix and .sh extension to frame it as a shell script, reinforcing the Unix-meets-Win95 aesthetic. Links to the affine matrix transformation game.

nodes.label: Desktop Icon: $izePAINT
nodes.description: Desktop icon positioned to the right of the //game.sh icon in the upper area. Icon image is a palette/paint-brush icon with warm orange/yellow tones. Label reads '$izePAINT' — uses a dollar-sign prefix ($ like a shell variable or currency symbol) combined with 'PAINT' evoking MS Paint. This likely links to the goose art upload feature.

nodes.label: Desktop Icon: c:\vibes
nodes.description: Desktop icon on the left column, second row. Label reads 'c:\vibes' — using Windows drive path notation (C:\) combined with the slang term 'vibes', blending retro Windows file path syntax with modern internet culture. Icon appears to be a small folder or file icon.

nodes.label: Desktop Icon: .skynet
nodes.description: Desktop icon on the right column, second row. Label reads '.skynet' — using the Unix dotfile prefix (hidden file convention) combined with 'skynet' (Terminator AI reference). Icon appears to show a small building or tower image. Cultural mash-up of Unix hidden files, Terminator lore, and Win95 aesthetics.

nodes.label: Desktop Icon: ...vote_.(gs)
nodes.description: Desktop icon in the lower-left area of the desktop. Label reads '...vote_.(gs)' — ellipsis prefix suggesting a truncated or mysterious path, 'vote' describing the voting feature, '_.' as separators, and '(gs)' likely referencing 'geese' or the goose theme. Small icon with what appears to be a landscape/image thumbnail. Links to the goose art voting carousel.

nodes.label: Desktop Icon Grid Layout
nodes.description: Icons are arranged in a loose two-column grid on the upper-left quadrant of the desktop, following classic Win95 icon placement convention. Left column: //game.sh (top), c:\vibes (middle), ...vote_.(gs) (bottom). Right column: $izePAINT (top), .skynet (middle). Icons have text labels beneath them in white/light text against the wallpaper.

nodes.label: Icon Label Typography Style
nodes.description: All desktop icon labels use small white text rendered directly over the wallpaper without a drop shadow or background pill, consistent with Win95 icon label rendering. Label text uses a mix of shell/terminal naming conventions: ./ prefix, // prefix, $ prefix, c:\ path notation, dotfile prefix, and parenthetical suffixes.

nodes.label: Overall Color Scheme
nodes.description: Color palette dominated by the wallpaper: vibrant green (grass), bright blue (sky), white (clouds). Taskbar is dark charcoal/near-black providing contrast. Icon images use warm yellows, oranges, greens. Text is white. The palette evokes both Windows XP nostalgia and a slightly surreal, whimsical aesthetic.

nodes.label: Win95 Desktop Metaphor
nodes.description: The entire UI uses the Win95/WinXP desktop metaphor: wallpaper background, desktop icons with labels, and a bottom-anchored taskbar with a start button. This is a deliberate retro-computing aesthetic choice for a modern web application, creating nostalgic UX.

nodes.label: Unix/Terminal Naming Convention for Icons
nodes.description: A distinctive design pattern where all desktop icon labels and the start button use Unix/terminal naming conventions (./, //, $, c:\, dotfiles, .sh extensions, parenthetical suffixes) rather than plain English labels. This creates a fusion aesthetic of Win95 GUI and Unix command-line culture.

nodes.label: Affine Matrix Game Feature (via //game.sh)
nodes.description: The //game.sh icon on the desktop represents the affine matrix transformation game, one of the core features of GooseOS. Accessible from the desktop as a clickable icon.

nodes.label: Goose Art Voting Feature (via ...vote_.(gs))
nodes.description: The ...vote_.(gs) icon on the desktop represents the goose art voting carousel feature, where users can vote on uploaded goose art. Accessible from the desktop as a clickable icon.

nodes.label: Goose Art Upload Feature (via $izePAINT)
nodes.description: The $izePAINT icon on the desktop likely represents the goose art upload feature, referencing MS Paint as a metaphor for art creation/upload. The paint palette icon reinforces this.

nodes.label: Fire Nation Goose Voting Carousel
nodes.description: Screenshot of the GooseOS goose art voting carousel shown inside a Win95-style window titled 'belles-lettres.exe'. Displays three horizontally arranged photos of geese/birds interacting with people in outdoor settings. The name 'fire-nation' derives from the visible caption text 'everything changed when the fire nation attacked', a pop-culture reference (Avatar: The Last Airbender meme) used as humorous alt-text or caption for the goose imagery. The UI features left/right chevron navigation arrows for cycling through goose art submissions, and two small icon buttons below (likely upvote/flag controls). The window uses classic Windows 95 chrome: gray title bar, minimize/maximize/close buttons in the top-right corner. The desktop background is flat gray and the taskbar at the bottom shows a '/start' button, consistent with the Win95 aesthetic of GooseOS.

nodes.label: belles-lettres.exe Win95 Window
nodes.description: The Win95-style application window containing the goose voting carousel. Titled 'belles-lettres.exe', referencing fine arts/literature in a tongue-in-cheek naming convention for a goose art gallery. Has standard Win95 window chrome: title bar, minimize/maximize/close buttons.

nodes.label: Goose Art Voting Carousel Component
nodes.description: The core UI component visible in this screenshot: a horizontally scrollable carousel displaying three goose art photos side by side, with left/right chevron navigation arrows and vote controls below. Implemented in legacy frontend using js/vote/carousel.js (D3.js or jQuery based).

nodes.label: Fire Nation Caption Meme Text
nodes.description: Visible caption text reading 'everything changed when the fire nation attacked' — a well-known internet meme referencing Avatar: The Last Airbender, applied humorously to describe goose aggression imagery in the carousel. This text names the screenshot file 'fire-nation.png'.

nodes.label: Win95 Desktop Taskbar with /start Button
nodes.description: Bottom taskbar element of the GooseOS desktop showing a '/start' button, consistent with the Windows 95 desktop metaphor applied throughout GooseOS. Uses command-style naming (/start) blending Win95 aesthetics with CLI/terminal aesthetics.

nodes.label: GooseOS Affine Matrix Game Screenshot
nodes.description: Screenshot of the affine matrix transformation game running inside a Win95-style window titled 'Goose.exe'. The game viewport is a white-bordered black rectangle centered in the window. A small white pixel-art goose/llama character is visible near the center of the viewport. Two 3x3 affine transformation matrices are displayed inside the viewport in monospace text: one on the lower-left and one on the lower-right. The matrices represent the current transformation state of the game. Outside the viewport (top-left of the window body) are three HUD stats: 'coordinates: -37, 37', 'time: 00:00:04.373', and 'matrices: 2'. Three red heart icons are displayed in the top-right corner of the window body, indicating the player has 3 lives remaining. The OS taskbar at the bottom shows a './start' button, mimicking the Win95 Start button. The desktop background is a blurred green field with blue sky, consistent with a Win95 aesthetic.

nodes.label: Player Character (Pixel-Art Goose/Llama)
nodes.description: A small white pixel-art character resembling a goose or llama, positioned near the center of the black game viewport. The sprite is minimal — roughly 10-15 pixels tall — consistent with a retro lo-fi visual style. It is the player-controlled entity navigating the affine transformation space.

nodes.label: Affine Transformation Matrix (Left)
nodes.description: A 3x3 affine transformation matrix displayed in monospace text in the lower-left area of the game viewport. Values read approximately: [[-1.41, 1.12, -7.00], [-1.45, -1.44, -39.00], [0.00, 0.00, 1.00]]. Displayed in orange/amber monospace font. Represents one of the two active transformation obstacles or waypoints in the game world.

nodes.label: Affine Transformation Matrix (Right)
nodes.description: A 3x3 affine transformation matrix displayed in monospace text in the lower-right area of the game viewport. Values read approximately: [[-0.38, -0.68, 15.00], [0.98, -0.54, 26.00], [0.00, 0.00, 1.00]]. Displayed in orange/amber monospace font. Represents the second active transformation matrix in the current game state.

nodes.label: HUD Stats Display (Coordinates, Time, Matrices)
nodes.source_location: top-left of window body, outside viewport
nodes.description: Three lines of HUD text displayed in small white monospace font outside the game viewport in the upper-left of the Win95 window body: 'coordinates: -37, 37' (player's current position in transformation space), 'time: 00:00:04.373' (elapsed game time showing precision to milliseconds), 'matrices: 2' (the count of active affine matrices currently present in the game). These metrics communicate the player's spatial state and game progression.

nodes.label: Lives Display (Heart Icons)
nodes.description: Three red heart icons arranged horizontally in the top-right corner of the Win95 window body (outside the game viewport). They indicate the player currently has 3 lives remaining. The heart design is simple and bold, consistent with the retro pixel-art aesthetic of the game.

nodes.label: Win95-Style Game Window (Goose.exe)
nodes.description: The entire game runs inside a Win95-style window with a blue title bar reading 'Goose.exe' and the standard minimize/maximize/close buttons (shown as box icons) in the top-right corner of the title bar. The window sits on a Win95-style desktop with a green-field-and-blue-sky wallpaper. A taskbar is visible at the bottom with a './start' button, a terminal-inspired twist on the classic Windows 'Start' button. The window is not maximized — it occupies most of the desktop area but leaves some desktop visible around it.

nodes.label: Game Viewport Canvas (Black Rectangle)
nodes.description: The game's rendering canvas is a solid black rectangle outlined with a thin white border, centered within the Win95 window. The black background provides high contrast for the white pixel-art character and the amber/orange matrix text. The canvas represents the affine transformation game world where all game objects and matrices are rendered.

nodes.label: Visual Style: Retro Win95 + Matrix Math Aesthetic
nodes.description: The game deliberately blends two retro aesthetics: (1) Win95 desktop UI chrome (title bar, taskbar, window decorations, classic wallpaper) and (2) a math/terminal aesthetic inside the viewport (black background, monospace matrix notation, pixel-art character). The orange/amber matrix text evokes old CRT terminal displays. The overall design communicates that the game's core mechanic is mathematical — affine transformations — while wrapping it in nostalgic desktop OS chrome for ironic/playful effect.
nodes.norm_label: visual style: retro win95 + matrix math aesthetic

nodes.label: Core Game Mechanic: Affine Matrix Navigation
nodes.description: The game's core mechanic involves navigating a player character through a 2D space defined by affine transformation matrices. The 'matrices: 2' counter and two visible 3x3 matrices suggest that matrices appear as entities in the game world (obstacles, targets, or portals). The player's position is tracked as a 2D coordinate (-37, 37), and elapsed time is measured with millisecond precision. Interaction with matrices likely applies the transformation to the player's coordinate space, altering movement, orientation, or scale — a mechanic unique to the affine game concept described in the codebase.
nodes.norm_label: core game mechanic: affine matrix navigation

nodes.label: No-Gods Screenshot — Goose Voting Carousel
nodes.description: Screenshot of the GooseOS goose art voting carousel. Displayed inside a Win95-style window titled 'belle-lettres.exe', the UI shows a 3-panel meme-style collage of Canada geese with overlaid text captions: 'He attacc' (repeated three times) and 'But most importantly'. Below the image carousel are left/right navigation arrows and a caption reading: 'one goose dared to love. All he ever wanted was a warm embrace... but fate made him a weapon'. The Windows 95 taskbar with a Start button is visible at the bottom of the screen. The overall color palette is gray/muted, consistent with Win95 desktop styling.

nodes.label: Goose Art Voting Carousel UI
nodes.description: The voting carousel component visible in the screenshot. Allows users to browse goose art submissions using left/right arrow navigation. Each item shows an uploaded image with an associated caption/description. Implemented in carousel.js as part of the GooseOS legacy frontend.

nodes.label: belle-lettres.exe Win95 Window
nodes.description: A Win95-style window frame wrapping the voting carousel, titled 'belle-lettres.exe'. Rendered by the GooseOS window manager system. Includes standard Win95 chrome: title bar with minimize/maximize/close buttons, gray bordered window body.

nodes.label: 'He Attacc' Goose Meme Submission
nodes.description: A user-submitted goose art piece displayed in the voting carousel. Composed of three photos of Canada geese attacking / charging, with meme-style caption text overlaid: 'He attacc' (top), 'He attacc' (middle), 'But most importantly' (bridge), 'He attacc' (bottom). Accompanied by the flavor text: 'one goose dared to love. All he ever wanted was a warm embrace... but fate made him a weapon'. This is the content displayed in the 'no-gods' screenshot state.

nodes.label: Silly Goosing Screenshot
nodes.description: Win95-style desktop screenshot showing the GooseOS voting carousel window titled 'ballot-lottery.exe'. nodes.label: Upload Goose Art UI (More Goose Window)
nodes.description: Win95-style desktop window titled 'upload.cmd' containing the goose art upload form. The window has standard Win95 chrome (minimize, maximize, close buttons). The inner panel is titled 'More Goose' in a monospace/pixel font. The form contains: (1) a dashed-border dropzone area labeled '[dropzone]' for drag-and-drop file input, (2) a text input field labeled 'describe:' with placeholder text 'yield thine ballads of galactic conquest...', and (3) two side-by-side buttons: 'browse' (file picker trigger) and 'upload' (form submission). The taskbar at the bottom shows a './start' button. Overall background is a classic Win95 desktop with blue sky and green hills wallpaper.
nodes.norm_label: upload goose art ui (more goose window)

nodes.label: Drag-and-Drop File Dropzone
nodes.description: A rectangular dashed-border dropzone component within the upload form. Labeled '[dropzone]' in monospace text at its center. Used for drag-and-drop image file upload of goose art. No preview content is visible in this state, indicating no file has been dropped yet.

nodes.label: Goose Art Description Text Input
nodes.description: A single-line text input field below the dropzone, labeled 'describe:'. Placeholder text reads 'yield thine ballads of galactic conquest...' in a humorous, lore-appropriate style. Allows the user to add a caption or description to their uploaded goose art.

nodes.label: Browse File Button
nodes.description: A Win95-style push button labeled 'browse'. Positioned to the left of the 'upload' button. Triggers the native file picker dialog to allow the user to select a local image file for upload.

nodes.label: Upload Submit Button
nodes.description: A Win95-style push button labeled 'upload'. Positioned to the right of the 'browse' button. Submits the selected image and description to the backend POST /upload endpoint.

nodes.label: Win95 Window Chrome (upload.cmd)
nodes.description: Standard Win95-style window frame with a blue title bar displaying 'upload.cmd' and three window control buttons (minimize, maximize, close) in the top-right corner. The window is rendered on a classic Win95 desktop background (blue sky, green hills).

nodes.label: Vibes Page - CRT TV Channel Viewer
nodes.description: The Vibes feature in GooseOS is an ambient TV channel viewer rendered as a Win95-style windowed application. The window title bar reads 'CRT.tv' with standard Win95 minimize/maximize/close controls in the upper right. The entire interface is styled as a retro CRT television set rendered in 3D perspective against a teal/sky-blue gradient background with a green grass strip at the bottom, evoking the classic Windows desktop wallpaper aesthetic. The television is a large tan/beige boxy CRT unit occupying most of the window. The screen displays heavy static/noise with full-spectrum RGB color interference lines running vertically — suggesting an untuned or between-channels TV signal. Faintly visible through the static is ghosted dark content, possibly a previously viewed video frame, giving the impression of a real analog TV struggling to receive a signal. Overlaid on the static in bright green terminal-style text is what appears to be a channel identifier or stream label, partially legible as something like 'cybertv.tv' or similar. The right side panel of the TV body contains the physical controls: a black rotary 'channel' dial (large, prominent, round) and a smaller 'power' button below it, both rendered as 3D skeuomorphic widgets. There are also several small square buttons or indicators stacked vertically to the left of the channel dial, resembling preset channel buttons. The bottom of the GooseOS window shows the Win95-style taskbar with a './start' button in the lower left. The overall visual atmosphere is lo-fi, nostalgic, and glitchy — intentionally evoking the experience of watching late-night cable TV on an old CRT set with poor reception.
nodes.norm_label: vibes page - crt tv channel viewer

nodes.label: CRT Television Skeuomorphic Widget
nodes.description: The central UI element is a photo-realistic or heavily styled illustration of a vintage boxy CRT television set. It features a curved screen displaying static noise, a tan/beige plastic housing, ventilation grille on the right panel, and physical-style controls including a large rotary channel selector dial and a power button. The 3D perspective rendering gives it depth and realism within the flat browser window context.

nodes.label: RGB Static Noise Screen Effect
nodes.description: The TV screen renders full-spectrum RGB vertical static interference lines, simulating an analog CRT television signal with no reception or between channels. The noise pattern uses red, green, blue, yellow, cyan, magenta pixel columns in a dense interference pattern. Ghost imagery is faintly visible beneath the static, suggesting a video stream attempting to load or a lossy/degraded video signal. This serves as the ambient visual content for the Vibes feature.

nodes.label: Channel Rotary Dial Control
nodes.description: A large black circular rotary dial labeled 'channel' on the right side panel of the CRT TV widget. This is an interactive control that likely switches between different ambient stream channels or video feeds in the Vibes feature. It is styled as a physical knob with a 3D appearance, consistent with the skeuomorphic CRT TV design.

nodes.label: Power Button Control
nodes.description: A smaller circular button labeled 'power' located below the channel dial on the right panel of the CRT TV widget. Likely toggles the TV on/off or activates/deactivates the stream playback. Styled to match the physical knob aesthetic of the overall CRT TV design.

nodes.label: Win95 Window Title Bar - CRT.tv
nodes.description: The Vibes feature is presented inside a Win95-style window with a title bar reading 'CRT.tv'. The title bar uses the classic blue gradient style with white text. Standard window control buttons (minimize, maximize, close) appear in the upper right corner, consistent with the GooseOS Win95 desktop theme implemented via window-manager.js.

nodes.label: Green Terminal Channel Label Overlay
nodes.description: Overlaid on the static noise in bright green monospace terminal-style text is a channel name or stream identifier. The text is partially legible through the interference, appearing to read something like 'cybertv.tv' or a similar retro internet/streaming channel name. This overlay reinforces the lo-fi aesthetic and suggests the Vibes feature streams from specific named internet channels or ambient video URLs.

nodes.label: Win95 Desktop Background - Sky and Grass
nodes.description: Visible behind the CRT TV illustration is the GooseOS Win95-style desktop background featuring a teal-to-light-blue sky gradient at the top and a solid green grass strip at the bottom. This is the standard GooseOS desktop wallpaper that appears across the application, providing environmental context for the floating window.
nodes.norm_label: win95 desktop background - sky and grass

nodes.label: Win95 Taskbar with ./start Button
nodes.description: The bottom of the screenshot shows the GooseOS Win95-style taskbar. The './start' button appears in the lower left, styled in the classic Windows 95 Start button format but with a terminal/Unix aesthetic twist using './' prefix notation, referencing shell command syntax. The taskbar is rendered with the characteristic raised 3D border style of Win95.
